explanation: King of Babylon, who conquered and destroyed Jerusalem and led the Jews into exile.
An ancient kingdom in Northeast Africa, often in conflict with the people of Israel and other nations in the region.
The longest river in Africa and a vital resource for Egyptian civilization.
Rulers of ancient Egypt, often regarded as gods by their people.
An organized military force, used here to refer to both Egyptian and Babylonian forces.
A symbol of war and destruction, frequently used in prophetic texts to describe God's judgment against nations.
A title often used for God in the Old Testament, especially when He acts with justice and judgment.
God's act of punishing nations for their sins and rebellion against His will.
Another way to refer to God, emphasizing His close relationship with Israel and their ancestor Jacob.
A period during which the people of Israel were taken captive and lived in a foreign land as a consequence of their disobedience to God.
